documents.title: Ratios and Rates Practice
documents.directions: Show your work. Circle your final answer.

questions.prompt: The shelter has 4 cats and 7 dogs. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?
questions.why: Dogs come first, so it is 7 : 4. 4 : 7 is cats to dogs, and 11 is the total, not a part.

questions.prompt: Match each sentence to its ratio.
questions.why: The first thing named comes first in the ratio. "Out of 5 pets" compares a part to the whole.

sections.heading: Level 2: Tape diagrams and unit rates

questions.prompt: The tape diagram shows the ratio of cats to dogs at a pet show. There are 30 animals in all. How many dogs are at the show?

questions.why: There are 5 equal parts in all, and 30 ÷ 5 = 6 animals in each part. Dogs have 3 parts: 3 × 6 = 18.

questions.prompt: A pet store sells 3 bags of fish food for $12. At this rate, how much do 5 bags cost?
Mia's dog eats 2 cups of food for every 5 miles they walk. Leo's dog eats 3 cups for every 8 miles. Find the cups of food for each mile for both dogs. Whose dog eats more food for each mile?
questions.why: Mia's dog: 2 ÷ 5 = 0.4 cups for each mile. Leo's dog: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 cups for each mile. 0.4 is more than 0.375.

questions.prompt: A dog treat recipe uses 3 cups of oats for every 2 eggs. Jada has 9 cups of oats and 5 eggs. How many eggs does she need to use all 9 cups of oats? Does she have enough? Explain.
questions.answer: She needs 6 eggs. 9 cups is 3 times the 3 cups in the recipe, so she needs 3 × 2 = 6 eggs. She has only 5, so she does not have enough.
questions.why: Look for the scale factor (9 ÷ 3 = 3), then use it on the eggs. A strong answer names the 6 eggs and compares it with the 5 she has.

documents.title: Ratios Quiz
documents.directions: Show your work. Circle your final answer.

sections.heading: Part 1: Ratio language and equivalent ratios

prompt.A: A vet sees 5 rabbits and 8 birds. What is the ratio of rabbits to birds?
prompt.B: A groomer has 6 poodles and 7 beagles. What is the ratio of beagles to poodles?

why.A: Rabbits are named first, so 5 : 8. 13 is the total.
why.B: Beagles are named first, so 7 : 6. 13 is the total.
3 × 3 = 9, but 4 × 3 = 12, not 16. Both parts must be multiplied by the same number.

prompt.A: A ratio table for puppy formula shows 1 scoop : 2 cups of water, 2 scoops : 4 cups, 3 scoops : 6 cups. How many cups of water go with 5 scoops?
prompt.B: A ratio table for kitten formula shows 1 scoop : 3 cups of water, 2 scoops : 6 cups, 3 scoops : 9 cups. How many cups of water go with 4 scoops?

prompt.A: A turtle walks 12 feet in 4 minutes. How many feet does it walk each minute?
prompt.B: A snail crawls 20 inches in 5 minutes. How many inches does it crawl each minute?

prompt.A: A kennel uses 4 bags of food every 6 days. At this rate, how many bags does it use in 15 days?
prompt.B: A shelter uses 6 bags of litter every 9 days. At this rate, how many bags does it use in 21 days?

why.A: 4 bags in 6 days is 2 bags in 3 days. 15 days is 5 groups of 3 days, so 5 × 2 = 10 bags.
why.B: 6 bags in 9 days is 2 bags in 3 days. 21 days is 7 groups of 3 days, so 7 × 2 = 14 bags.

prompt.A: Store 1 sells 4 chew toys for $10. Store 2 sells 6 chew toys for $14. Which store has the lower price for each toy?
prompt.B: Shop 1 sells 3 leashes for $21. Shop 2 sells 5 leashes for $34. Which shop has the lower price for each leash?

why.A: Store 1: $10 ÷ 4 = $2.50 each. Store 2: $14 ÷ 6 ≈ $2.33 each. Store 2 is lower.
why.B: Shop 1: $21 ÷ 3 = $7.00 each. Shop 2: $34 ÷ 5 = $6.80 each. Shop 2 is lower.

findings.what: Two answers fit. With only 1 : 3 and 2 : 6 shown and a jump to 4 scoops, the blind tester read the table as "add 3 each row" and picked 9.
findings.before: 1 scoop : 3 cups, 2 scoops : 6 cups. How many cups go with 4 scoops?
findings.fixed: Added a third row so the pattern can only be read one way. The key (12) did not change.
findings.after: 1 scoop : 3 cups, 2 scoops : 6 cups, 3 scoops : 9 cups. How many cups go with 4 scoops?

findings.what: "Eats more food per mile" was read as more food in all, and the blind tester answered Leo's dog.
findings.before: Whose dog eats more food per mile?
findings.fixed: Reworded to ask for the cups of food for each mile first, then compare.
findings.after: Find the cups of food for each mile for both dogs. Whose dog eats more food for each mile?

findings.what: Flagged that a true/false question can be guessed half the time.
findings.reason: Kept on purpose: one true/false per version, and the same skill is tested again in q3.

findings.what: The right answer was the longest choice in 2 of 5 multiple-choice questions, so the longest-choice bot scored 40%, over the 35% line.
